newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland wants EMU sanctions for fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: Finland wants EMU sanctions for fiscal discipline.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Thursday Finland supported the idea of sanctions to enforce fiscal discipline once the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) had started.

Reiterating Finland's objective to bring its public sector deficit into surplus in relation to gross domestic product when EMU starts in 1999, he told a seminar that other single currency countries, too, should exercise strict budgetary discipline.
"The credibility of EMU and the Euro, and of Euro interest rates, will depend decisively on expectations for how the balance of public finances will develop," he said.
It was therefore important to define the rules and the sanctions for fiscal policy, Niinisto said.
"Finland supports the strengthening of the credibility of the single currency through rules of conduct," he said.
Finland also wanted to retain sufficient flexibility in national economic policy, he added, but did not elaborate.

A so-called budgetary stability pact and the legal framework for the Euro will be on the agenda of a September 9-10 meeting of the EU Monetary Committee and at an informal ECOFIN Council meeting of EU finance ministers in Dublin September 20-22.

An official ECOFIN Council meeting in Luxembourg on October 14 will prepare issues relating to the EMU third stage for the October 22 European Council meeting of heads of state and government in Dublin.
